name: 3D-DNA
description: 3D de novo assembly (3D-DNA) pipeline for Hi-C data genome scaffolding.

name: ABRA2
description: ABRA2 is an updated implementation of ABRA featuring RNA support, improved scalability, accuracy, and stability.

name: ABRicate
description: Mass screening of contigs for antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes.

name: ABySS
description: A de novo, parallel, paired-end sequence assembler designed for short reads.

name: AdapterRemoval
description: AdapterRemoval trims adapter sequences and low quality bases from High-Throughput Sequencing (HTS) data in FASTQ format.

name: ADMIXTOOLS
description: ADMIXTOOLS is a software package primarily used for analyzing admixture in population genetics. It implements methods described in Patterson et al. (2012) for demographic history inference.

name: ADMIXTURE
description: ADMIXTURE is a software tool for maximum likelihood estimation of individual ancestries from multilocus SNP genotype datasets.

name: Alevin
description: A tool for efficient quantification and analysis of 3' tagged-end single-cell RNA-seq data.

name: AliView
description: AliView is a fast and lightweight alignment viewer and editor for large data sets.

name: ALLHiC
description: ALLHiC: phasing and scaffolding polyploid genomes based on Hi-C data

name: AlphaFold
description: AlphaFold uses artificial intelligence to predict protein structures with high accuracy, solving a decades-long challenge in biology. It has predicted over 200 million protein structures, which are freely available through the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database.

name: AMBER
description: A suite of biomolecular simulation programs for biomolecular dynamics, developed by the AMBER community.

name: Ancestry_HMM
description: A hidden Markov model approach for simultaneously estimating local ancestry and admixture time using next generation sequence data in samples of arbitrary ploidy.

name: ANGSD
description: A software for analyzing next generation sequencing data, handling input types from mapped reads to imputed genotype probabilities.

name: ANNOgesic
description: ANNOgesic is a command-line tool for RNA-Seq based annotation of bacterial/archaeal genomes, serving as a "Swiss army knife" for detecting genes, CDSs, TSSs, transcripts, sRNAs, and more.

name: AnnotSV
description: An integrated tool for structural variations annotation and ranking

name: antiSMASH
description: antiSMASH allows the rapid genome-wide identification, annotation and analysis of secondary metabolite biosynthesis gene clusters in bacterial and fungal genomes.

name: Anvi'o
description: Anvi'o is an open-source platform for microbial 'omics analysis and visualization, supporting genomics, metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, pangenomics, metapangenomics, phylogenomics, and population genetics.

name: ARACNe
description: ARACNe (Algorithm for the Reconstruction of Accurate Cellular Networks) is a novel algorithm using microarray expression profiles designed to scale up to regulatory networks in mammalian cells, using an information theoretic approach to eliminate indirect interactions.

name: ARAGORN
description: Trna and tmrna detection in nucleotide sequences

name: ARB
description: ARB is a graphical software environment for sequence database handling and analysis, providing tools for phylogenetic studies and rRNA sequence data management.

name: ARIBA
description: ARIBA is a bioinformatics tool for identifying antibiotic resistance genes via local assembly of sequencing reads. It supports MLST calling and requires reference sequences and paired-end reads as input.

name: Arriba
description: Arriba is a fast tool to search for aberrant transcripts such as gene fusions. It is based on chimeric alignments found by the STAR RNA-Seq aligner.

name: arrow
description: Arrow: Better dates and times for python

name: ARTIC
description: artic is a pipeline and set of accompanying tools for working with viral nanopore sequencing data, generated from tiling amplicon schemes. Features include read filtering, primer trimming, amplicon coverage normalisation, variant calling, and consensus building.

name: artic-porechop
description: Adapter removal and demultiplexing of Oxford Nanopore reads (fork of rrwick/Porechop)

name: ASTRAL
description: ASTRAL is a tool for estimating an unrooted species tree given a set of unrooted gene trees. ASTRAL is statistically consistent under the multi-species coalescent model (and thus is useful for handling incomplete lineage sorting, i.e., ILS).

name: Augur
description: Augur is the bioinformatics toolkit we use to track evolution from sequence and serological data. It provides a collection of commands which are designed to be composable into larger processing pipelines.

name: Augustus
description: A program for predicting genes in eukaryotic genomic sequences. It supports RNA-Seq integration, retrainability, prediction of alternative splicing and UTRs, and incorporation of extrinsic evidence such as ESTs and protein alignments. The tool is open-source and can be run locally or via a web interface.

name: auspice
description: An open-source interactive web app for visualizing phylogenomic data, part of the Nextstrain project.

name: AutoDock
description: A suite of automated docking tools designed to predict how small molecules bind to receptors of known 3D structure.

name: Bakta
description: Bakta is a tool for the rapid & standardized annotation of bacterial genomes and plasmids from both isolates and MAGs. It provides dbxref-rich, sORF-including and taxon-independent annotations in machine-readable JSON & bioinformatics standard file formats for automated downstream analysis.

name: BamM
description: Metagenomics-focused BAM file manipulation

name: bam-readcount
description: Count bases in BAM/CRAM files.

name: BamTools
description: C++ API & command-line toolkit for working with BAM data.

name: BamUtil
description: These files provide some programs for working on SAM/BAM files.

name: Bandage
description: Bandage is a GUI program that allows users to interact with the assembly graphs made by de novo assemblers such as Velvet, SPAdes, MEGAHIT and others.

name: Barrnap
description: Barrnap predicts the location of ribosomal RNA genes in genomes (bacteria, archaea, metazoan mitochondria, and eukaryotes).

name: Battenberg
description: Battenberg is a tool built atop of Cookiecutter to keep Cookiecut projects in sync with their parent templates. It uses Git for merging, diffing, and conflict resolution.

name: BBTools
description: BBTools is a suite of fast, multithreaded bioinformatics tools designed for analysis of DNA and RNA sequence data. BBTools can handle common sequencing and bioinformatics file formats such as fastq, fasta, sam, bam, scarf, fasta+qual, gff, gtf, vcf, and gzip/bgzip/bzip2 compressed files.

name: bcbio-nextgen
description: Validated, scalable, community developed variant calling, RNA-seq and small RNA analysis

name: bcftools
description: BCFtools is a set of utilities that manipulate variant calls in the Variant Call Format (VCF) and its binary counterpart BCF. All commands work transparently with both VCFs and BCFs, both uncompressed and BGZF-compressed.

name: bcl2fastq
description: bcl2fastq is used for demultiplexing sequencing data and converting BCL files generated by Illumina sequencing systems into FASTQ format for downstream analysis.

name: Beagle
description: Beagle is a software package for phasing genotypes and imputing ungenotyped markers, with version 5.5 offering improved memory efficiency and accuracy for large sequence datasets.

name: BEAST2
description: BEAST2 is a cross-platform program for Bayesian phylogenetic analysis of molecular sequences. It estimates rooted, time-measured phylogenies using strict or relaxed molecular clock models.

name: bedGraphToBigWig
description: Converts bedGraph files to bigWig format.

name: BEDOPS
description: BEDOPS is a suite of tools to address common questions raised in genomic studies — mostly with regard to overlap and proximity relationships between data sets.

name: bedtools
description: bedtools - the swiss army knife for genome arithmetic. The most widely-used tools enable genome arithmetic: that is, set theory on the genome. For example, bedtools allows one to intersect, merge, count, complement, and shuffle genomic intervals in BED, GFF, VCF, and BAM formats.

name: Bellerophon
description: Bellerophon is a genetic optimization tool for Approximate Computing (AC). It is meant for use in collaboration with clang-Chimera.

name: Bifrost
description: Highly parallel construction and indexing of colored and compacted de Bruijn graphs

name: biobambam
description: Tools for early stage alignment file processing

name: biobambam2
description: A collection of tools for early stage alignment file processing, including bamsort for sorting BAM files by coordinate or query name.

name: bioconductor-maxcontrastprojection
description: Perform a maximum contrast projection of 3D images along the z-dimension into 2D

name: bioconductor-unifiedwmwqpcr
description: Unified Wilcoxon-Mann Whitney Test for testing differential expression in qPCR data

name: biomaRt
description: biomaRt provides an interface to a growing collection of databases implementing the BioMart software suite. The package enables retrieval of large amounts of data in a uniform way without the need to know the underlying database schemas or write complex SQL queries.

name: biopet-validateannotation
description: Validateannotation validates whether an annotation file is correct.

name: Bismark
description: Bismark is a program to map bisulfite-treated sequencing reads to a genome of interest and perform methylation calls in a single step. It supports single-end and paired-end read alignments, both ungapped and gapped alignments, and allows adjustable parameters such as alignment seed length and number of mismatches. The output can be easily imported into genome viewers like SeqMonk.

name: BLASR
description: BLASR (Basic local alignment with successive refinement) is a tool for mapping single-molecule sequencing reads against a reference genome.

name: BLAST
description: BLAST+ is a suite of command-line tools for performing sequence alignment and database searching. It offers improved performance through multithreading and includes new features such as sequence filtering applications (segmasker, dustmasker, windowmasker).

name: BLAT
description: BLAT is a fast sequence search tool for rapid alignment of mRNA/DNA and cross-species protein sequences.

name: Blobtools
description: Modular command-line solution for visualisation, quality control and taxonomic partitioning of genome datasets

name: BMGE
description: Bmge (block mapping and gathering with entropy) is a program that selects regions in a multiple sequence alignment that are suited for phylogenetic inference.

name: bmtagger
description: Best Match Tagger for removing human reads from metagenomics datasets.

name: BOLT-LMM
description: BOLT-LMM computes statistics for testing association between phenotype and genotypes using a linear mixed model (LMM). BOLT-REML estimates heritability and genetic correlations among multiple traits.

name: Bowtie
description: An ultrafast memory-efficient short read aligner

name: Bowtie2
description: Bowtie2 is an ultrafast and memory-efficient short read aligner for aligning sequencing reads to long reference sequences, particularly effective for reads of 50 to 1,000s of characters and for aligning to long genomes like the human genome. It uses an FM Index to keep memory usage low (e.g., ~3.2 GB for the human genome) and supports gapped, local, and paired-end alignment modes.

name: Bracken
description: Bracken (Bayesian Reestimation of Abundance with Kraken) is a highly accurate statistical method that computes the abundance of species in DNA sequences from a metagenomics sample.

name: BRAKER2
description: BRAKER2 is a fully automated pipeline for eukaryotic genome annotation using RNA-Seq data and protein homology information to predict protein-coding genes accurately.

name: BRASS
description: BRASS is a bioinformatics tool that identifies breakpoints and attempts to assemble rearrangements in whole genome sequencing data.

name: Breseq
description: A computational pipeline for finding mutations relative to a reference sequence in short-read DNA re-sequencing data for haploid microbial-sized genomes.

name: BRIG
description: BRIG is a cross-platform (Windows/Mac/Unix) application that displays circular genome comparisons. It handles genome assembly data, performs BLAST comparisons automatically, and shows contig boundaries and gene presence/absence.

name: BSMAP
description: BSMAP is a short reads mapping software for bisulfite sequencing reads.

name: BS-Seeker2
description: BS-Seeker2 is a versatile pipeline for bisulfite sequencing data mapping.

name: BURST
description: BURST (formerly known as embalmer) is an optimal, high-speed pairwise sequence aligner specialized in aligning many NGS short reads against large reference databases.

name: BUSCO
description: BUSCO (Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs) is a tool for assessing the completeness of genome assemblies, transcriptomes, or gene sets based on evolutionarily informed expectations of gene content from near-universal single-copy orthologs.

name: bustools
description: Bustools is a program for manipulating BUS files for single cell RNA-Seq datasets.

name: BWA
description: Burrow-Wheeler Aligner for short-read alignment (see minimap2 for long-read alignment)

name: bwa-mem2
description: bwa-mem2 is the next-generation version of BWA-MEM, providing the same alignment results with 1.3-3.1x speed improvement.

name: bwa-meth
description: Fast and accurate alignment of BS-Seq reads.

name: CADD
description: CADD (Combined Annotation-Dependent Depletion) is a computational tool for scoring the pathogenicity of genetic variants. It integrates multiple annotations to predict the deleteriousness of variants across the human genome.
